newsitem.title: THAILAND: FORECAST-Thai 1997 exports seen up 6.0 pct-TFRC.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Thai 1997 exports seen up 6.0 pct-TFRC.

text.p: Thai exports are expected to grow by 6.0 percent in 1997 following an 0.2 percent contraction in 1996, a research group said on Wednesday.
Thai Farmers Research Center (TFRC), a unit of Thai Farmers Bank Plc, said exports this year were expected to total 1.462 billion baht ($58.48 million), against 1.379 billion baht in 1996.
The projected export rise was lower than the central bank's forecast of 7.2 percent growth. In 1995, exports grew by 23.6 percent.
TFRC said imports in 1997 were expected to widen one percent from last year to 1.815 billion baht.
Thailand has suffered a sharp export slowdown. Economists have forecast decade-low economic growth of 5.9 percent in 1997, against 6.4 percent growth in 1996.
The country's finance sector is troubled with over-exposure to the depressed, cash-strapped and glutted property sector and current high interest rates have stifled businesses.

TFRC said the country's gross domestic product (GDP) was expected to grow 5.3 percent in 1997 compared to 6.4 percent in 1996. It also projected this year's consumer price index to rise 4.6 percent against 5.9 percent last year.
It said the country's current account deficit in 1997 would narrow to 310 billion baht compared to 372.6 billion last year.
Commercial bank loans were expected to grow 11 percent this year versus 14.2 percent in 1996 while deposit growth was seen at 12 percent compared to 13.7 percent in 1996, it said.
